storylines.label: Reasoning Latent
storylines.latest_title: [AINews] Behind Latent Space: Kill My SaaS, Jev & AI in 2026 | AIEi Shanghai

prior_narrative.tldr: An Oct 18 paper proposed hybrid agents that reason in latent space but act through text. A paper on Oct 27 then applied latent reasoning to multi-agent systems by storing reusable skills in compact external memory.
prior_narrative.whats_new: A new arXiv paper moves latent reasoning into continuous space for unified multimodal models, targeting weak language-based chain-of-thought in image tasks.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Latent reasoning aims to cut inference cost by keeping intermediate steps out of text, but it also makes those steps harder to inspect and log.

beats.headline: Hybrid agents think in latent space, act through text
beats.summary: Separates internal reasoning from the textual action interface.

beats.headline: SkillMem stores skills externally for latent multi-agent systems
beats.summary: Targets the mismatch between continuous reasoning and text-supplied skills.

beats.headline: Latent reasoning extends to unified multimodal models
beats.summary: Applies continuous-space reasoning to image understanding and generation.

open_questions: Do any of these papers report cost or latency savings against text chain-of-thought on the same tasks?
Is code or a model release available for the Hybrid Agents or SkillMem approaches?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: These are unreplicated preprints; if you log reasoning traces for debugging, check what your tooling would lose before adopting latent-reasoning models.

storylines.latest_title: Verda Inference, in Preview with Kimi K3.1 Pro

prior_narrative.tldr: Latent Space's Oct 7 newsletter put Claude Haiku 5.5 ahead of GPT-6 Luna at the same pricing. On Oct 20, Google Cloud added Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 to its Antigravity coding tool.
prior_narrative.whats_new: R&D World compares Kimi K3.1 Pro against Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra (Oct 23); only the headline is in the item, so the results are not confirmed here.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Claude 5.5 models are reaching more surfaces (Antigravity), and a Chinese open-weight lab is now being benchmarked against Opus 5.5, so model-routing choices are being re-opened.

status.detail: Claude 5.5 models are spreading to new platforms while Kimi K3.1 Pro is being compared against them; no outcome is confirmed in these items.

Is Kimi K3.1 Pro available via a public API, and at what price?
Do independent evals confirm Haiku 5.5 beating GPT-6 Luna at equal pricing?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you route between models, rerun your own evals with Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3.1 Pro as candidates before changing defaults, and treat the Haiku 5.5 vs Luna claim as unverified until you test it.

storylines.label: MCP Servers
storylines.latest_title: AI coding agents are installing abandoned MCP servers with known security issues

prior_narrative.tldr: On Nov 1 a benchmark post reported a 17-point gap between agents running the same model across 21 MCP servers, putting the client side of MCP under scrutiny. On Nov 2 a Show HN project proposed cryptographic identity for agents calling MCP servers.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Uber built an MCP Gateway to govern agent access to more than 800 MCP servers and 5,000 tools, separating tool registration from runtime execution.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: MCP is moving from per-server wiring to centrally governed infrastructure, and results depend on the agent client as much as the model or server.

status.detail: Threads on MCP agent variance, agent identity and enterprise gateways are emerging together.

beats.headline: Same model, different agent: 17 points apart on 21 MCP servers
Arken proposes cryptographic identity for agents calling MCP servers
Uber centralizes access behind an MCP Gateway

open_questions: Will other large engineering orgs publish MCP gateway designs for discovery, auth and auditing?
Will the 17-point agent-client gap be reproduced on other MCP server sets?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Pin the agent client alongside the model in MCP evals, and check whether tool registration, auth and audit are centralized before your server count grows.

storylines.label: DeepSeek Open-sources
storylines.latest_title: DeepSeek Open-Sources Super-Agent, a Coding Agent That Works From Team Chat

prior_narrative.tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer on Oct 20, the inference software behind its production models, first framed as a way to cut AI operating costs and then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic. Oct 21 coverage added the 155T tokens-a-day serving scale and a high serving margin.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Nov 2: TechNode, TNGlobal and Help Net Security describe DeepSeek's dsh-superagent as a proactive research prototype, a coding agent that watches team chats for work.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Two open DeepSeek releases in two weeks, a serving stack and a coding-agent architecture, give platform teams reference designs to benchmark their own inference and agent harness against.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public and unreproduced; dsh-superagent is described as a research prototype with no independent results yet.

beats.headline: Earlier adjacent items clustered before the release
beats.summary: Not DeepSeek coverage: a web-agent distillation paper (Oct 14) and a mixed-hardware inference framework (Oct 18).

beats.headline: DeepSeek ties V4.1-Flash-1017 to its own Harness (Oct 17)
beats.summary: Groundwork for the later Harness-team releases.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources the stack that runs its models
beats.summary: Bloomberg, Quartz, Gizmodo and PYMNTS report the release on Oct 20 as an open-source tool to lower AI operating costs.

beats.headline: SiliconANGLE names it DeepInfer, the framework behind production services
Scale and margin figures arrive
beats.summary: Latent Space and follow-up writeups cite 155T tokens a day and a high-margin serving business.

beats.headline: DeepSeek's Harness team open-sources dsh-superagent, a router-worker coding agent
beats.summary: Hacker News links the GitHub architecture on Oct 31; Nov 1 coverage frames it as a challenge to Claude Code; Nov 2 reports call it a proactive research prototype that watches team chats.

beats.headline: Later unrelated items in the window
beats.summary: Not DeepSeek coverage: llm-d 1.0 (Oct 20), agent, evaluation, multi-agent, compression and retrieval papers (Oct 21-Nov 2), inference-engine essays and demos (Oct 24, Oct 31, Nov 2, Nov 3), and a quantization paper (Oct 29).

open_questions: Does an independent benchmark reproduce the 155T tokens/day and ~80% margin figures?
Which license terms govern commercial reuse of DeepInfer and dsh-superagent?
Does dsh-superagent's bug-fixing claim hold on an independent coding benchmark?
Does dsh-superagent run on models other than DeepSeek's own?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer and dsh-superagent repos and licenses before borrowing designs; treat the margin and bug-fixing claims as unverified until someone reproduces them outside DeepSeek's stack.

prior_narrative.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 15 it has gathered an O-RAN benchmark, agentic-RL training papers on rollout cost and credit assignment, and AWS's SageMaker multi-turn guide.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Agent RL is now judged on cost and reliability: EnvSched and calibrated budgets (Oct 20) target rollout spend, while MiRL and CalibraRL target named failures. All are paper-reported results, not production evidence; the SageMaker guide remains the only managed-platform recipe.
open_questions: Does calibrated rollout budgeting cut MCP-agent training cost on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does the SageMaker MTRL recipe carry from Wordle to tool-using agent tasks, and at what training cost?
Do MiRL's error-targeted fixes hold on terminal-agent tasks outside the paper's own benchmark?
Does EnvSched's scheduling gain hold on agent-RL benchmarks beyond the paper's own, and with which environment mixes?
Does TalentRL's strategy-guided routing beat flat SkillBank retrieval on agent benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does EffComp's compression ratio hold quality on downstream tasks beyond the paper's own benchmarks?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using agents, measure rollout cost per environment (EnvSched, calibrated budgets), log recurring failure modes for error-targeted RL (MiRL), and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat paper results as unreplicated until rerun on your own evals.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Nov 2: two arXiv papers add EffComp, a hybrid RL-plus-supervised prompt compressor aimed at cheaper LLM calls, and an axiomatic framework for RL in open multi-agent systems.

status.detail: A loose set of RL items; the newest add prompt compression and multi-agent theory to the agent rollout-cost, credit-assignment and reliability work.

prior_narrative.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models", so most of it is a reading list, not one thread. Oct 16-28 items cover sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, steering and continual learning, and Mistral Large 4 shipped Oct 29.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Nov 2: Anthropic reported progress on zkSNARK-based provable inference, and InfoQ argued agentic architectures need a context engine that selects, injects, compresses and expires information.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Mistral Large 4 is the one deployable item: vLLM support landed with the weights. The newest items point at architecture choices: how agents manage context and memory, and how inference might be verified.
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you self-host, pull Mistral Large 4 on the vLLM day-0 build and rerun your own evals before swapping it in. For agents, audit where context is selected, compressed and expired in your harness before adding more memory.

prior_narrative.tldr: Earlier Qwen 3.8 coverage centered on benchmark claims for the 27B open-weight build. In mid-October, OrcaRouter published four comparison pieces that set other models against Qwen 3.8 (UserRepGen-4B, Beam 1.0, Glimpse, Dory 1.0 4B).
prior_narrative.whats_new: On Nov 3, Simon Willison reported that Qwen 3.8 27B running on his laptop can interpret model weights, tied to the Sparks of Weight-Space Programming paper.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Qwen 3.8 27B is now a baseline other vendors position against, and a laptop-sized open model is being used for weight-level interpretability experiments.

status.detail: Qwen 3.8 appears mostly as a comparison point, with one new hands-on interpretability result.

Do any of the OrcaRouter comparisons publish benchmark numbers against Qwen 3.8?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you use Qwen 3.8 27B locally, rerun the weight-reading experiment on your own checkpoint before relying on it, and treat vendor comparison posts as unverified until they cite benchmark scores.

prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Two harness-versus-model posts in three days make the same point: the agent harness can move results as much as the model, so evaluate the full stack.

status.detail: Title-match papers are coincidental; the Nov 1 and Nov 3 posts form the real thread on harness effects.
